Rashi on Shabbat 109a:10:1.hebrew: רבי יוסי אומר כל הימים - וים הגדול, תורת מעיין מים זוחלין עליהן לענין שהם מטהרין בזוחלין, מפני שדרך להיות נחלים זוחלין עליהן וזה דרכן. אבל פסולין הן לתורת מים חיים, דהכתוב קראן מקוה:
Rashi on Shabbat 109a:10:1.english: Rabbi Yosei says: All seas - and the Great Sea [as well]: the law of a spring of flowing water applies to them with respect to their purifying while flowing, because streams normally flow into them and this is their nature. However, they are invalid with respect to the law of living water, for Scripture called them a mikveh.

Rashi on Shabbat 109a:1:1.english: Into a barrel - Into which they put beer.

Rashi on Shabbat 109a:1:10.english: Causes the Daughter of the King to pass - If she harmed his eyes.

Rashi on Shabbat 109a:1:2.english: Should be severed - So that [the hand] should not touch [the body] before the morning washing [of hands].

Rashi on Shabbat 109a:1:3.english: A hand - [put] to the eye causes blindness before washing [one's hands].

Rashi on Shabbat 109a:1:4.english: A hand - [placed] to the ear causes deafness.

Rashi on Shabbat 109a:1:5.english: A hand - [put] to the mouth or to the nose.

Rashi on Shabbat 109a:1:6.hebrew: מעלה פוליפוס - ריח החוטם והפה. ול"נ דיד לאמה לאו לענין שחרית נקט לה, אלא משום דמביא לידי קרי, ובמסכת נדה (דף יג:) אמרינן בה תקצץ משום האי טעמא, ומשום דתניא בה נמי לטותא דתיקצץ, תנייה נמי גבי הנך. וכן יד לפי טבעת — למשמש בה תדיר מביאתו לידי תחתוניות:
Rashi on Shabbat 109a:1:6.english: Causes polypus - [Bad] odor of the nose and the mouth. And it seems to me that [the case of] "a hand to the membrum" was not stated with respect to [unwashed hands in] the morning, but rather because it leads to a seminal emission, and in Tractate Niddah (13b) we say concerning it, "Let it be severed," for this reason; and because a curse of "let it be severed" was taught concerning it as well, [the Tanna] taught it together with these [others]. And similarly, [concerning] "a hand to the anus" — touching it constantly brings one to hemorrhoids.

Rashi on Shabbat 109a:1:7.english: She is a free woman - [This refers to] the spirit that rests on the hands before washing.

Rashi on Shabbat 109a:1:8.hebrew: ומקפדת - בנטילתו לנוטלה יפה, עד שישפוך מים יפה ג' פעמים על ידיו:
Rashi on Shabbat 109a:1:8.english: And she is particular - regarding his removing [her], to remove her properly, until he pours water properly three times over his hands.

Rashi on Shabbat 109a:1:9.english: Eye shadow - If one puts it in his eyes.

Rashi on Shabbat 109a:2:1.english: Leaves [alin] - That is the name of the herb.

Rashi on Shabbat 109a:2:2.hebrew: אין בהם משום רפואה - באכילתו להאיר העינים, דלא מסו:
Rashi on Shabbat 109a:2:2.english: They contain no element of healing - [with regard to] eating it to brighten the eyes, for they do not heal.

Rashi on Shabbat 109a:2:4.hebrew: אפילו לדידי - דמאור עינים אנא, קשה לי לכאב העין אם אוכלנו:
Rashi on Shabbat 109a:2:4.english: Even for me - For I am blind, [yet] it is harmful to me, [causing] eye pain if I eat it.

Rashi on Shabbat 109a:2:6.hebrew: אפילו לדידי - דמאור עינים אנא, מעליא לי:
Rashi on Shabbat 109a:2:6.english: Even for me - For I am blind [lit. of light of eyes], [and yet] it is beneficial for me.

Rashi on Shabbat 109a:2:7.hebrew: כל מיני כשות שרי - למיכל בשבת, כדתנן במתני': כל האוכלים אוכל אדם לרפואה, דלא מוכחא מילתא:
Rashi on Shabbat 109a:2:7.english: All types of hops are permitted - to be eaten on Shabbat, as we learned in the Mishnah: "A person may eat any foods for healing," since it is not evident [that it is for healing].

Rashi on Shabbat 109a:2:8.english: Except for teruza - For a person only eats [it] for healing, and the matter is evident.

Rashi on Shabbat 109a:3:1.hebrew: שריקא טויא - לשרוק ולטוח שמן וביצים מגולגלין על הצלי כשהוא חם משחשכה, שרי, ובלבד שלא יהא רותח כדי לבשל, ולא אמרינן דמי למתקן:
Rashi on Shabbat 109a:3:1.english: Smearing a roast [sherika tavya] - To smear and spread oil and soft-boiled eggs onto the roast while it is hot after dark is permitted, provided that it is not boiling hot enough to cook [them], and we do not say [that] it resembles improving [the food].

Rashi on Shabbat 109a:3:2.english: Beating eggs - To beat soft-boiled eggs in a bowl.

Rashi on Shabbat 109a:3:3.english: Is forbidden - For it looks like one who wants to pour them into a pot.

Rashi on Shabbat 109a:3:4.english: She made for him - sherika tavya [a basted roast].

Rashi on Shabbat 109a:3:6.english: A strainer - [That] with which one strains dregs.

Rashi on Shabbat 109a:3:7.english: Since it is drunk like this - [That is,] it is fit to be drunk as it is, without straining.

Rashi on Shabbat 109a:3:8.english: That it is eaten like this - [The roast is fit to be eaten even] without basting.

Rashi on Shabbat 109a:4:1.hebrew: שנגפה - שנכשלה ולקתה, לשון "פן תגוף" (תהילים צ״א:י״ב), "דם מגפתה" (מכשירין פ"ו מ"ח):
Rashi on Shabbat 109a:4:1.english: That was wounded - That stumbled and was struck; an expression [like] "lest you strike [your foot]" (Psalms 91:12), [and] "the blood of her wound" (Makhshirin 6:8).

Rashi on Shabbat 109a:4:2.english: Stanches it in wine - to abate the blood.

Rashi on Shabbat 109a:4:3.hebrew: דמפנקי - מעונגין הן, וכל דבר שהוא חזק קצת קשה לבשרן וצומתה:
Rashi on Shabbat 109a:4:3.english: [Since] they are delicate - They are pampered, and anything that is somewhat strong is harsh for their flesh and contracts [the wound].

Rashi on Shabbat 109a:5:1.english: That a donkey stepped on him - A donkey stepped on his foot.

Rashi on Shabbat 109a:5:2.english: Are different - For its wound is severe and dangerous, and one may desecrate the Shabbat for it.

Rashi on Shabbat 109a:7:1.hebrew: רוחצין במי גרר - ואע"פ שהן מלוחין קצת, דרך לרחוץ בהן בחול, ולא מוכחא מילתא דלרפואה היא:
Rashi on Shabbat 109a:7:1.english: One may bathe in the waters of Gerar - Even though they are somewhat salty, it is customary to bathe in them on weekdays, and it is not evident that it is for medicinal purposes.

Rashi on Shabbat 109a:7:2.english: However, not in the Great Sea - Later [the Gemara] explains the reason.

Rashi on Shabbat 109a:7:3.hebrew: ולא במי משרה - ששורין בו פשתן, ואין דרך רחיצה בהן אלא לרפואה דמסו. וכן בימה של סדום, דמליח טובא ואין רוחצין בה אלא לרפואה, ומוכחא מילתא:
Rashi on Shabbat 109a:7:3.english: Nor in soaking water - in which they soak flax, and it is not customary to bathe in them except for healing, as they heal. And similarly in the Sea of Sodom, for it is very salty and one does not bathe in it except for healing, so the matter is evident.

Rashi on Shabbat 109a:9:1.hebrew: הא - דקתני רוחצים בים הגדול, ר"מ היא, דמשוי כל הימים כי הדדי ולא מפליג בין ים הגדול לשאר הימים:
Rashi on Shabbat 109a:9:1.english: This - [the baraita] that teaches [that] one may bathe in the Great Sea is [the view of] Rabbi Meir, who equates all seas to one another and does not distinguish between the Great Sea and other seas.

Rashi on Shabbat 109a:9:2.hebrew: והא - דתני אין רוחצין, רבי יהודה היא, דמפליג בין ים הגדול לשאר ימים:
Rashi on Shabbat 109a:9:2.english: And that [one] - which teaches "one may not bathe," is [the opinion of] Rabbi Yehuda, who distinguishes between the Great Sea and other seas.

Rashi on Shabbat 109a:9:3.hebrew: כל הימים כמקוה - לכל תורת מקוה, ואין להם תורת מעיין. ומה בין מקוה למעיין? המעיין כשר לטבילת זב, והזאת צפור מצורע — דמים חיים הן — ולקדש מי חטאת, דבכולהו "מים חיים" כתיב: בזב כתיב (ויקרא ט״ו:י״ג) "ורחץ בשרו במים חיים", במצורע כתיב (שם יד) "אל כלי חרס על מים חיים", במי חטאת כתיב (במדבר י״ט:י״ז) "מים חיים אל כלי". ומטהר טמאים הטובלים במימיו כשהן זוחלין ומקלחים, שהרי זה דרכו של מעיין — כל עצמן זוחלין הן. ומקוה, שהן מים מכונסין, אם הטביל במימיו דרך זחילתן במקום קטפרס, אינה טבילה, עד שיהא במקום אשבורן שלו, קווין ועומדין. והכי תניא בתורת כהנים: "אי מה מעיין מטהר בזוחלין, אף מקוה מטהר בזוחלין? ת"ל 'אך מעיין' — מטהר בזוחלין, והמקוה באשבורן". זהו פירוש "מטהר בזוחלין" בכל מקום, ואני לא שמעתיו כן. ואין המקוה כשר לטבילת זב, ולהזיית מצורע, ולקדש מי חטאת. וכל הימים כמקוה, שהכתוב קראן "מקוה":
Rashi on Shabbat 109a:9:3.english: All seas are like a mikveh - With respect to all the laws of a mikveh, and they do not have the status of a spring. And what is [the difference] between a mikveh and a spring? A spring is valid for the immersion of a zav, and for the sprinkling of the bird [of] a metzora — for they are living waters — and to sanctify the waters of purification [for the red heifer], for in all of them "living water" is written: regarding a zav, it is written (Leviticus 15:13), "and he shall bathe his flesh in living water"; regarding a metzora, it is written (ibid. 14), "into an earthenware vessel over living water"; regarding the waters of purification, it is written (Numbers 19:17), "living water into a vessel." And [a spring] purifies impure [people or vessels] that immerse in its waters while they are flowing and streaming, for this is the nature of a spring — by their very nature they are flowing. Whereas a mikveh, which is gathered water — if one immersed in its waters while they are flowing on a slope [katafres], it is not a [valid] immersion, until [the water] is in its basin [ashboren], collected and standing. And thus it was taught in Torat Kohanim: "Just as a spring purifies while flowing, might a mikveh also purify while flowing? The verse states: 'However, a spring' [Leviticus 11:36] — [a spring] purifies while flowing, whereas a mikveh [purifies only] when collected in a basin." This is the explanation of "purifies while flowing" in every place, though I did not hear it thus. And a mikveh is not valid for the immersion of a zav, nor for the sprinkling of a metzora, nor to sanctify the waters of purification. And all seas are like a mikveh, because Scripture called them "a gathering [mikveh]."

Rashi on Shabbat 109a:9:4.hebrew: רבי יהודה אומר - לא קרא הכתוב מקוה אלא לים הגדול, דביה משתעי קרא במעשה בראשית, ששם נקוו כל מי בראשית:
Rashi on Shabbat 109a:9:4.english: Rabbi Yehuda says - Scripture only called the Great Sea mikveh [a gathering of waters], for the verse speaks of it in [the account of] Creation, since all the waters of Creation were gathered there.

Rashi on Shabbat 109a:9:5.hebrew: ולא נאמר ימים - בלשון רבים, אלא מפני שמעורבין בו מיני ימים הרבה, שכל הנחלים הולכים אל הים:
Rashi on Shabbat 109a:9:5.english: And "seas" was not stated - in the plural, except because many kinds of seas are mixed in it, for "all the streams flow into the sea."

Tosafot on Shabbat 109a:10:1.hebrew: רבי יוסי אומר כל הימים מטהרין בזוחלין - נראה לריב"א דטעמא משום דכל שעה הולכים ושבים מכאן לכאן, והוי כזוחלין; הלכך יש להם לטהר בזוחלין כמו שאר נהרות. אבל מים חיים אינם, שהרי אינם נובעים; הלכך מיסתבר טפי: מה שהכתוב קראן מקוה — היינו לפוסלן ממים חיים:
Tosafot on Shabbat 109a:10:1.english: Rabbi Yosei says: All seas purify when flowing - It appears to Riva that the reason is because at every moment they go back and forth from here to there, and [thus] they are like flowing [waters]; therefore, they should purify when flowing like other rivers. However, they are not living water, since they do not spring forth; therefore, it is more reasonable [that] what Scripture called them "a gathering [of water]" (mikveh) is to disqualify them from [counting as] living water.

Tosafot on Shabbat 109a:2:1.hebrew: עלין אין בהם משום רפואה - פי' בקונטרס דבאכילה מיירי. ואין נראה לר"י, אלא איירי להשים על העין, דבהכי איירי כולה סוגיא. ועוד: אי באכילה מיירי, היכי אסר רב ששת גרגירא, כיון דמאכל בריאין הוא? והתנן: "כל האוכלים אוכל אדם לרפואה":
Tosafot on Shabbat 109a:2:1.english: Leaves contain no element of healing - [Rashi] explained in the Kuntres that [the Gemara] is speaking of eating [them]. But it does not appear [correct] to the Ri; rather, it is speaking of placing [them] on the eye, for that is what the entire sugya is discussing. And furthermore, if it is speaking of eating, how could Rav Sheshet forbid arugula, since it is a food of healthy people? Have we not learned [in a Mishnah]: "All foods a person may eat for healing"?

Tosafot on Shabbat 109a:2:2.hebrew: לדידי אפילו כוסברתא קשי לי - קשה לר"י: א"כ, אמאי איצטריך למימר רב יוסף "כוסברתא אין בו משום רפואה"? כיון דמזקת לעינים, כ"ש דלא מרפאה. ואומר ר"י דה"ק: "אין בה משום רפואה" — כלומר, יש שטועין וסבורין שיש בה רפואה, ואין בה רפואה, אלא מזקת לעינים, ויכול להיות שמהנה אותו בשום ענין:
Tosafot on Shabbat 109a:2:2.english: For me, even coriander is harmful to me - It is difficult for the Ri: If so, why did Rav Yosef need to say, "Coriander contains no element of healing"? Since it harms the eyes, all the more so it does not heal! And the Ri says that this is what he means: "It contains no element of healing" — that is to say, there are those who err and think that there is healing in it, whereas [in truth] there is no healing in it; rather, it harms the eyes, though it is possible that it benefits [the person] in some [other] respect.

Tosafot on Shabbat 109a:3:1.hebrew: שריקא טויא - פירש ר"ח: מים שמסננים ממעי אבטיח, ושותים כדי לשלשל. ור"ל דמותר לסנן מים שבמעיין, כדמסיק: "כיון דמיתכיל הכי — לאו מידי קעביד"; אבל פעפועי ביעי אסור, דלא מיתכיל בלא סינון שפיר. והשתא אתי שפיר לפי' ר"ח, דשייכא הא מלתא להכא, דמיירי ברפואה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 109a:3:1.english: Sherika tavya [melon juice] - Rabbeinu Chananel explained: [This is] water that is strained from the insides of a melon and drunk to act as a laxative. And he means to say that it is permitted to strain the water that is in its source [i.e., the melon's pulp], as [the Gemara] concludes: "Since it is consumed this way, he is not doing anything [forbidden]"; however, pi'pu'ei bei'ei is forbidden, because it is not consumed well without straining. And now it fits well according to Rabbeinu Chananel's explanation how this matter relates to here, where [the Gemara] is dealing with medicine.

Tosafot on Shabbat 109a:7:1.hebrew: רוחצין במי גרר במי חמתן במי טבריא - והא דתנן בפ' חבית (לקמן שבת דף קמז.): "הרוחץ במי מערה במי טבריא", ודייק בגמרא: דיעבד — אין, לכתחילה — לא; התם מיירי ברוחץ בגומא דדמיא למרחץ, אבל בנהר מותר לכתחילה, כדפרישית לעיל בפרק כירה (לעיל לט: ד"ת והא). ורבינו נסים כתב במגילת סתרים: דהא דקתני "הרוחץ", דיעבד אין לכתחילה לא — משום מי מערה, אבל במי טבריא אפילו לכתחילה שרי; ולא קתני "במי טבריא" אלא ללמד על מי מערה שהן חמין דומיא דמי טבריא. וטעמא: משום דמי טבריא מגולין, אבל מערה מכוסה היא, כדאמר בשור שנגח את הפרה (ב"ק דף נ:): דמערה עבידא דמטללא, ונפיש הבלא וחיישינן שמא יזיע, ומש"ה לכתחילה לא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 109a:7:1.english: One may bathe in the waters of Gerar, in the waters of Ḥamatan, [and] in the waters of Tiberias - And [as for] that which we learned in a Mishnah in the chapter [entitled] Chavit (later, Shabbat 147a): "One who bathes in cave water [or] in the waters of Tiberias," and the Gemara infers: after the fact — yes, [but] initially — no; there it is speaking of one who bathes in a pit, which resembles a bathhouse, whereas in a river it is permitted [even] initially, as I explained above in the chapter [entitled] Kirah (above 39b, s.v. Veha). And Rabbeinu Nissim wrote in Megillat Setarim that [the inference from] that which it teaches "One who bathes" — after the fact yes, initially no — is because of cave water, whereas in the waters of Tiberias it is permitted even initially; and it only teaches "in the waters of Tiberias" in order to teach regarding cave water that it is hot, similar to the waters of Tiberias. And the reason is because the waters of Tiberias are uncovered, whereas a cave is covered, as [the Gemara] says in [the chapter entitled] Shor SheNagach Et HaParah (Bava Kamma 50b): that a cave is typically roofed over, so the steam is abundant and we are concerned lest one perspire, and therefore [it is] not [permitted] initially.

Tosafot on Shabbat 109a:9:1.hebrew: הא ר"מ והא רבי יהודה - תימה: היכי מדמי הא פלוגתא לפלוגתא דלעיל, דמיירי ברפואה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 109a:9:1.english: This [is] Rabbi Meir, and that [is] Rabbi Yehudah - [It is] astonishing: how does [Rabbi Yochanan] compare this dispute to the dispute above, which deals with healing?
